rated_messages.input_message: Just because letting an urge pass isn't easy, doesn't mean that you can't do it. Try it, you might surprise yourself.
Each time you choose to not smoke after seeing someone else light up, you lessen the habit a little more.
Sometimes an urge comes on like a wave. Imagine what it is like to ride the wave as it ebbs and flows. Instead of trying to swim against it, try riding it out until it disappears into the sea.
Urges are like annoying ads. You might see them but you don't have to buy what they're selling.
A funny thing about people is that we tend to believe what we tell ourselves. So make sure that whatever else happens today, tell yourself "I can, and I will stick to not smoking!"

Spend 3 minutes noticing how your hands feel, how your mouth feels, and how your chest feels. The more you practice noticing these things without smoking, the sooner this place will stop being a trigger for you.
If you're stuck at home and physical activity doesn't interest you, try gaming, needlework, drawing, or journaling.
Pause. Notice what triggered you to smoke in the past. Now take one deep breath and remind yourself that you do not need to smoke.

Ask yourself, "What do I need right now? Is it really a smoke, or is there something else I need? How can I best take care of myself right now?"
Each time you let an urge pass without smoking, you break the old habit a bit more.
